subject: set XXH_REROLL=1 on gcc
perf_evidence: Code comment added: 'The if/then loop is preferable to switch/case on gcc (on x64)'; message 'but not on clang' - a per-compiler codegen/speed choice.
change_summary: Default XXH_REROLL becomes 1 when compiled by GCC (defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__)), selecting the rerolled while-loop tail of XXH32_finalize instead of the unrolled switch; doc comment updated.

units.name: XXH32_finalize rerolled loop vs switch (XXH32 one-shot len 0..31, streaming digest len 0,1,3,4,5,7,8,11,12,15), GCC preprocessor view emulated with -U__clang__, x86-64-v3
units.evidence: 42/42 targets fwd+bwd correct; old XXH_REROLL=0, new XXH_REROLL=1 (macro_check.txt); ir differs for every tail length != 0

notes: x86-64 IR unchanged under clang: all one-shot APIs (symbolic len) with -march=x86-64-v3 and default SSE2 give identical modules except !srcloc line metadata (x86_ident_v3/, x86_ident_sse2/). With real clang the change is invisible (XXH_REROLL=0 on both sides; module IR identical), so the configuration where it bites (GCC) was emulated by compiling with clang and -U__clang__ (clang still defines __GNUC__=4): the preprocessor then takes the GCC branch exactly as GCC would (macro_check.txt). Passing -DXXH_REROLL=1 to both sides would compare identical configurations and is meaningless. What is verified is the C-level equivalence of the two XXH32_finalize variants that GCC users now get; GCC's own codegen is not checked. Lengths are fixed (clang fully unrolls); since XXH32_finalize only depends on len&15 and the tail bytes, 0..31 covers every tail case on the unaligned one-shot path, and the streaming digests cover the aligned path for 10 tail lengths. Flags: -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 -fno-strict-aliasing -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize -w -U__clang__ -DXXH_NO_INLINE_HINTS=1 -mllvm -inline-threshold=100000; inputs as noundef scalars in a local buffer; asm guards -> freeze (64 rewrites each side, identical).
